pairs.subject: credential-vault
pairs.evidence: src/stores/slices/vault/credentialSlice.ts:363 an unreachable probe returns without recording the attempt in the store, and nothing in src/ reads the backend's persisted healthcheck_last_unreachable_at (src-tauri/src/engine/healthcheck.rs:680), so the last green ages behind a checkmark with no 'could not check since' beside it.

techniques.evidence: src/stores/slices/vault/credentialSlice.ts:363 verdict is correctly left alone on unreachable (and :389 maps a throw to unreachable), but the attempt is dropped instead of stored as a second fact; the verdict path (:377, and src-tauri/src/engine/healthcheck.rs:692) also never clears a prior unreachable attempt, which rev 4 requires of every verdict writer
src/stores/slices/vault/credentialSlice.ts:396 preview field values are session-encrypted before they cross IPC

pairs.registryProposal: Stale conformant (rev 2) flipped by rev 4's 'two facts stored as two + every verdict writer owes the clear' rule: the backend half here is realized (healthcheck.rs:680 writes the attempt) while the frontend half has zero readers, so the attempt exists on disk only. Worth naming in health-probing that a persisted attempt with no consuming surface is the same defect as dropping it.

pairs.subject: credential-vault
pairs.evidence: src-tauri/db/src/repos/resources/external_api_keys.rs:74 the app mints these keys itself and stores only a hash (:75); it is their issuer and verifier, never a holder of a foreign secret, and the golden path excludes secrets the application mints and owns.
pairs.registryProposal: This pair was added by a 2026-08-29 /conform triage as 'precondition governs', but the golden path's own exclusion (app-minted secrets; 'always the holder, never the minter of authority') says the opposite. An issued-API-key lifecycle (mint, one-time reveal at src/features/settings/sub_api_keys/components/CreatedKeyDialog.tsx:4, hash-at-rest, expiry, revoke) is governed by authorization or an issuer-side subject; the corpus may lack an issuer-side 'issued credentials' subject, which is a forge lead rather than a reason to keep this pair.

declined.subject: credential-vault
declined.reason: vault-credentials-manager is an orchestration shell; its rotation, retirement and acquisition behaviours resolve into the backend strategies and useUndoDelete outside the context. Reading only the shell gave one candidate (useRotateAll.ts:43 drops each rotation error to a bare count) but not the half-of-nine anchors a conformant needs, nor enough to call that drop a technique failure. Left unknown for a run that walks rotate_now end to end.
